newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold up on shortcovering.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold up on shortcovering.

text.p: Hong Kong gold ended higher on Wednesday over New York's Tuesday close on buying from Japanese traders on the Tokyo Commodity Exchange, dealers said.
"Japanese buying early this morning pulled the market up," said one gold trader.
Traders in Japan who were short were covering their positions, bullion dealers said.
Hong Kong bullion ended at US$369.20/70 an ounce on Wednesday against New York's US$368.40/80 close on Tuesday.
Pre-Christmas shortcovering would continue to push the market slightly higher, some traders said.
But Christmas holidays had thinned the crowd of bullion dealers and the market was illiquid, so that remaining players were reluctant to enter the field, bullion traders said.
Local gold ended HK$11 higher at HK$3,409 a tael.
Tael gold was trading at a premium to the spot market, with the U.S. dollar equivalent at $369.80/370.30.
"People are not as comfortable arbitraging between the spot and tael market since the premium has narrowed," one senior trader said.
But other dealers reported some tael sales and buying on the spot market.
The tael gold premium over spot gold was around $1 earlier this month when spot prices dropped sharply earlier this month.
The carryover charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society remained unchanged from its previous fix at -6.00.
